Subject: Trial recap & next steps — data handling notes

Samira, thanks again for the demo this morning — really appreciated the context on Healtronics' pilot. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned:

What we heard from you:
- Trial scope: 10K monthly queries, patient triage prompts + structured extraction.
- Hard constraints: no persistent storage of raw PII from prompts, US-only residency for any persisted artifacts, audit export for security review, and the ability to reduce retention to the shortest feasible TTL for trial.

What Redwood will provide for the trial:
- Default hosted trial environment scoped to us-east-1.
- Option to enable per-route TTLs and redaction rules.
- Preview SOC2 summary and a short privacy snippet for your security team to sign off (attached).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Confirm whether Healtronics needs exports in a specific format (CSV vs JSON) for audit.
2) Confirm desired max retention for any persisted artifacts during trial (suggested: 30 days or less).
3) If you want us to disable long-term prompt storage entirely for the trial, say so and we will turn on ephemeral mode for your account.

I attached the mutual action plan (trial-mop.xlsx) and the SOC2 summary. If you prefer, I can loop in Dev for a follow-up to walk through exact TTL and redaction behavior.

Thanks — Evelyn

Thanks, Evelyn — clear recap. A couple clarifying questions from our security/compliance reviewer before we sign the MOP:

1) When you say "disable long-term prompt storage entirely": does that mean prompt text and model outputs are never written to disk, or just that they are not copied to long-term object storage?
2) What is the TTL for any request/ingestion logs you keep (structured request metadata, timestamps, request IDs)?
3) Do you retain KV cache or session-level state beyond the request for continuity? If so, for how long and where is it stored (region)?
4) For exports: can we request an on-demand export of the trial activity logs and prompt outputs for the security review? If yes, what auth model do you use (S3 presigned vs. secure share)?

If you can answer those three points we can move forward. We prefer the shortest practical retention and US-only residency for anything persisted.

Evelyn / Marissa — answers below, written so you can paste them into an email to the customer. Ping me if they want a short tech call.

1) "Disable long-term prompt storage": for hosted trial accounts we can enable an "ephemeral capture" mode. In that mode:
   - Prompt text and model outputs are not persisted to our long-term object store (S3).
   - Short-lived in-memory buffers and a transient KV cache are used to serve streaming responses; those are kept in-memory on the serving node and flushed after session inactivity.
   - We do write minimal ingestion metadata (request id, timestamp, non-PII route tags) to a short-lived log store for observability.

2) TTL for logs/telemetry:
   - Default trial telemetry/log retention: 7 days (aggregated metrics retained longer for platform ops).
   - If Healtronics requires, we can reduce trial telemetry TTL to 3 days on request and document that change in the MOP.

3) KV cache / session state:
   - KV cache is ephemeral by design for hosted trials: session continuity uses an in-memory KV cache with a 1 hour idle eviction. Nothing from that cache is copied to replica or blob store.
   - Region: the trial environment will be provisioned in us-east-1 only.

4) Exports / auth model:
   - We support on-demand exports of trial activity (audit logs + optionally prompt outputs if the customer consents) via a temporary S3 export. We provide exports as either
     a) S3 presigned URL (short-lived), or
     b) secure transfer to a customer-provisioned S3 bucket via an IAM role we assume for the export.
   - All exports are delivered over TLS and logged for audit; we can add an export manifest for your security reviewer.

Attachments included for the customer: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (one-page), and a short "trial privacy snippet" you can paste into the MOP (attached as trial-privacy-snippet.txt).

Suggested reply to customer (paste-ready):
> Hi Samira — thanks for the questions. Short answers: we can enable an ephemeral capture mode so prompt text and outputs are not written to long-term object storage; session KV is in-memory and evicted after 1 hour of inactivity; trial telemetry defaults to 7 days but can be reduced to 3; we support on-demand exports via presigned S3 or customer-bucket transfer. All trial environments are provisioned in us-east-1. See attached SOC2 summary and privacy snippet.

- Marissa: please attach the latest SOC2 one-pager (attached) and add any legal caveats if needed.
